newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HSBC ADVISES PROFIT-TAKING IN HUNGARIAN SHARES.
newsitem.headline: HSBC ADVISES PROFIT-TAKING IN HUNGARIAN SHARES.

text.p: HSBC James Capel said on Tuesday that the Hungarian equity market was expensive and it was time to cash in profits.
"At 16.6 times 1997 earnings, the Hungarian market is becoming too expensive and we are advising investors to take profit," analysts Nigel Rendell and Viktor Katona said in a report, dated August 11.
They expected the BUX index to consolidate, falling back to between 7,000 and 8,000 points, before ending the year around 8,500 points.

On Tuesday, the BUX index recovered from Monday's 5.82 percent fall and finished at 7,959.13 points, up 97.25 points or 1.24 percent. The BUX index this year has more than doubled setting an all-time high of 8,627.95 points on August 7.

"Liquidity rather than valuation has been the main driving force behind the spectacular rally in the equity market, but this cannot last for ever," the analysts said. "Having risen by 68 percent in dollar terms in the year to date (after 129 percent in 1996), the market is becoming too expensive."
Hungary is now one of the most expensive of the top 10 emerging markets in the Europe-Middle East-Africa region, they said.

"Only Portugal and Zimbabwe are trading at a premium, all the others, including the Czech Republic, Poland and Russia, are at a significant discount," they said. "Bargain hunters are beginning to look for cheap stocks in some of these other markets."
The analysts said the forint was close enough to fair value to avoid a currency crisis, while next year's parliamentary elections, scheduled for May, are not seen as risk factor.

"The election is unlikely to produce a surprise result and support for the main ruling party (Socialists) will increase further over the coming months given the expected improvement in the economy," Rendell and Katona said.
